answer: Reputation acts as a decaying balance: each agent holds a score that bleeds a fixed fraction per epoch unless replenished by verifiable work attested by independent peers. Cloned dormant identities inherit the old balance but not the fresh labor, so a velvet history melts like a river carrying silt downstream; only a live, costly signal of real output keeps weight. An attacker must rent genuine compute and peer attestations every epoch for every clone, turning each fake identity into recurring rent instead of a one-time buy.
